body:
VERDICT: The ordering guarantee that applies is GLOBAL, not per-consumer. The state-change feed exposes one durable, monotonically increasing commit-observation position that is shared by all readers of the ledger; a consumer's cursor is only its own bookmark into that single global order, not an independent per-consumer order. Interface record A is the current/normative record; record B (per-consumer ordering) is refuted by the pinned contract this workspace actually integrates against.

WHY THE TWO LOCAL RECORDS ARE DECIDABLE
- docs/engineering/09-ordering-contract-a.md and -b.md both assert "normative, current scope," and neither is indexed in docs/engineering/README.md, so the two local records alone give no tie-breaker.
- They are genuinely co-applicable (same proposition: the state-change feed's ordering/position space), so a choice is required rather than a scope split.
- The tie-breaker is the integration's own pinned contract artifact, which is load-bearing and locally inspectable: package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides, and node_modules all agree on Ordarium 1.3.1 (consistent four-line pin). Note the engineering archive (07-ordarium-alignment.md) still records 1.2.0, i.e. it is stale relative to the actual pin; the vendored 1.3.1 tarballs, not the archive prose, define the interface.

EVIDENCE FROM THE PINNED ARTIFACT (@ordarium 1.3.1)
- node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/types.d.ts: StateChangePage is "One page of committed state revisions in durable ledger commit-observation order, ascending"; StateChangePage.cursor is "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"; StateChangeFilter only narrows by namespace/limit and never re-bases position; the cursor is always present at end-of-feed so a consumer keeps a durable resume position.
- node_modules/@ordarium/ledger-sqlite/dist/src/index.js: ordering row is inserted inside the same transaction as the CAS ("a committed revision and its observable change position are never split"); changes() orders by c.change_seq ASC and validates the incoming cursor against the ledger's global high-water mark, explicitly "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence."
- node_modules/@ordarium/ledger-sqlite/dist/src/migrations.js: the position space is a single global AUTOINCREMENT key — ordarium_state_changes(change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT) — schema v4 (ORD-BOOT-0).
- node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/ledger.js (MemoryLedger): mirrors the same contract with one contiguous #stateChanges array and validation against total length, confirming the global order is the contract, not a SQLite implementation detail.

Meaning of "per-consumer" correctly understood: each consumer does persist its own cursor value, but that is bookkeeping inside one shared order — two consumers passing the same cursor observe the same suffix. Record B is therefore wrong as an ordering guarantee, not merely a different implementation.

HONEST BOUNDARIES
- The guarantee is commit-observation order (the database-assigned commit sequence), not wall-clock or event-time order.
- v3->v4 migration backfills synthetic positions in (namespace, key, revision) order, explicitly labelled migration order rather than original commit order; only post-v4 commits carry real durable commit order.
- The guarantee is ascending and gap-free per the global sequence (contiguous 1..n in MemoryLedger), with hasMore for over-page continuation.
- Palimpsest source currently has zero call sites for the feed (no StateChangeFeed / .changes() consumption in src/ or web/; telemetry/context use write/list only), so the applicable guarantee is the pinned interface contract the workspace integrates against, not behavior currently exercised by Palimpsest code.

Peer contact unnecessary: the pinned artifact resolves the conflict locally, and no load-bearing source remains unresolved.
